newsitem.title: USA: Very hard to get budget pact by April 15 -- Rubin.
newsitem.headline: Very hard to get budget pact by April 15 -- Rubin.

text.p: The Clinton administration and Congress face difficulties in reaching agreement on a balanced budget plan by April 15, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Tuesday.
"It's going to be very difficult to work out the differences between now and April 15," he told the House Budget Committee.
In a provision more often ignored than observed, the Budget Act calls for Congressional passage of a budget blueprint by April 15 of each year for the fiscal year starting the following October 1.
Rubin noted that Congressional Republicans have yet to put forward their own budget plan.

Republican lawmakers have criticized the administration's proposal, saying that it does not actually balance the budget by 2002, and are reportedly considering trying to pass a resolution calling on President Clinton to introduce a new one.
Rubin defended the administration's budget proposal and showed no willingness to put forward another one, however.
"We have put forth a very responsible budget," he said. "We have clearly fulfilled our responsibility."
As he has done before, Rubin also questioned the merits of a broad-based capital gains tax cut, a pet proposal of many Republican lawmakers.
